stimulus.text: The photograph, taken on February 22, 1956, shows Rosa Parks being fingerprinted by Deputy Sheriff D. H. Lackey in Montgomery, Alabama, during the bus boycott. Parks, secretary of the Montgomery branch of the NAACP, had been arrested on December 1, 1955, for refusing to give up her bus seat to a white passenger. Black residents of Montgomery then refused to ride the city buses, walking or using carpools instead. The boycott lasted 381 days, ending on December 20, 1956, after the Supreme Court affirmed that bus segregation was unconstitutional.

stem: The photograph was taken during which event?

options.misconception: Background from the books: the March on Washington came in 1963, years after this 1956 photograph.
Background from the books: the Little Rock crisis came in September 1957, after this photograph.
Background from the books: the Freedom Rides began in 1961, years after this photograph.

rationales.A: Background from the books: the March on Washington came in 1963, years after this 1956 photograph.
rationales.B: Background from the books: the Little Rock crisis came in September 1957, after this photograph.
rationales.C: Background from the books: the Freedom Rides began in 1961, years after this photograph.
rationales.D: The photograph is dated February 1956, in the middle of the boycott that Parks's arrest began.
rationales.general:
1. The photograph shows Parks being fingerprinted by a Montgomery deputy in February 1956.
2. The stimulus says her arrest on December 1, 1955, began a boycott of the city buses.
3. A February 1956 booking photograph falls inside that boycott, which ran from December 1955 to December 1956.
Remember: a photograph's date places it inside the event it belongs to.
